quotes.text: You have 7 calendar days after the dispute is created to submit evidence.
Connected accounts must have the `scalapay_payments` capability enabled.
Stripe immediately notifies you whether the payment succeeded or failed.

old_evidence.text: You must submit the requested information within 12 calendar days.
Other categories at the discretion of Scalapay
The maximum charge limit is 4,999,99 EUR or the equivalent for other supported currencies.

findings: November is a full method overview. Use the one-time B2C payment flow, with merchant or qualifying Connect account type, provisional access, supported account and customer geography, eligible category and EUR range. Dashboard enablement or manual integration navigation is not acceptance. Checkout Sessions/full-page is recommended; the product surface includes Payment Intents, Payment Links, embedded form, Payment Element and in-app. Recurring, Setup Intents, Payment Intents with future usage, Checkout setup/subscription mode, and Express Checkout Element are unsupported (old 8-53, 85-113, new 9-22, 43-62, 129-143, 206-238, 262-266).

The buyer selects Scalapay, redirects to the hosted provider page, selects three or four installments and authorizes. At the November overview's depicted payment-complete step, the buyer sees confirmation and returns, and Stripe immediately reports success or failure. After success the merchant can read latest_charge.payment_method_details.scalapay.transaction_id on a PaymentIntent. Standard payout schedule still applies, and no browser return establishes success or external payout on its own (old 20-34, 95-101, new 9-14, 240-260).

November lists manual and partial capture, with multi/overcapture and named extended/incremental/decremental/re-authorization options unsupported. May method overview already marks manual capture. The separate May acceptance guide shows authored requires_capture and cancellation after seven days on that route (raw/stripe-scalapay-accept-payment-2025.md:1094-1103,1122-1138). Do not re-date that seven-day capture period or treat it as the dispute evidence deadline (old 43-46, new 132-143 and 175-190).

Full or partial refund submitted within 90 days, processing nominally up to five minutes, final Refund succeeded or failed by status/event, and failed amount returned to Stripe balance with obligation to refund another way remain in scope. November additionally describes full refund canceling remaining installments and returning paid amounts, partial refund adjusting the plan. November opens full disputes once within 210 calendar days from purchase, Stripe immediately withholds the balance, merchant evidence is due in seven calendar days with one submission, provider decision is within 30 calendar days, and win restores the hold while customer win makes charge permanent (old 127-158, new 145-204).

Root index line 7 goes to Stripe index 342-349 and 745-749. The BNPL concept 156-168 and 266-267 includes both method and acceptance; existing source lines 27-29 only route to old raw. Keep the index/concept inbound links and restore reciprocal BNPL and acceptance navigation. Preserve separate versioned Android announcement scope (concept 233-237).

The separately read BNPL product matrices change Scalapay Mobile Payment Element from Unsupported (raw/stripe-bnpl-overview-2025.md:40,49) to Supported (raw/stripe-payments-buy-now-pay-later-2026-11-07.md:41,50). The November dedicated Scalapay overview also labels in-app payments Supported (new raw lines 206-213). The aggregate product row, dedicated in-app row and versioned Android announcement in BNPL concept lines 233-237 describe separate scopes and do not prove a particular SDK integration or account enablement. Scalapay remains absent from the aggregate API matrix.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/scalapay the November 7 article describes single-use B2C installments, provisional activation subject to geography, category and risk, and domestic/cross-border EUR payments from 5.00 to 4,999.99 EUR within the listed markets. The merchant and buyer lists are separate. Connect platforms can act for connected accounts with scalapay_payments enabled. The buyer redirects to Scalapay, chooses three or four installments and authorizes. At the November overview’s depicted payment-complete step, Stripe reports success or failure immediately and the merchant can retrieve a transaction ID after success (new raw lines 240-260). November separately lists manual and partial capture (new raw lines 139-143). The May acceptance guide’s manual route leaves a successful authorization in requires_capture until the merchant explicitly captures it, within a documented seven-day window (May acceptance guide lines 1094-1103 and 1122-1136). Browser return after authorization does not establish completion for fulfillment. Standard payout timing is separate. The dedicated overview supports this capture route, with recurring/setup, future usage, multicapture and overcapture excluded. The 90-day refund updates installments and ends in succeeded or failed; a failure returns the amount to Stripe balance and requires another way to refund. A customer may file one full dispute within 210 calendar days, Stripe withholds the amount, the merchant has seven calendar days to submit one evidence packet, and a merchant win restores the held balance while a buyer win makes the charge permanent. May showed a broader EU buyer label, a list of 28 merchant countries, No Connect and 12 days for evidence. source-stripe-scalapay.md still gives the May limits and should be dated and corrected (old raw lines 8-53, old raw lines 52-93 and old raw lines 121-158, compared with new raw lines 9-62, new raw lines 129-204 and new raw lines 206-266).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/scalapay, update source-stripe-scalapay.md with the nine November buyer countries (AT, BE, DE, ES, FI, FR, IT, NL and PT) and separate merchant geography. The merchant list adds CY, EE, HR, LI, LV and MT and omits May’s HU. Keep EUR presentment and the exact 4,999.99 EUR charge maximum, alongside the rounded 5,000 EUR option rows. Connect capability, prohibited categories with residual risk, and the shift from 12 to seven calendar days for dispute evidence are substantive. Preserve May’s dedicated No Connect versus its aggregate Supported label, the separately dated Checkout acceptance scope and authorized-capture window, and the unchanged 90-day refund lifecycle with new installment detail (old raw lines 35-38, old raw lines 52-83, old raw lines 115-158, new raw lines 18-62, new raw lines 68-127, new raw lines 145-204 and new raw lines 206-238). The separately captured May BNPL product matrix marks Mobile Payment Element Unsupported, while November marks it Supported (May BNPL raw lines 40 and 49, November BNPL raw lines 41 and 50). The dedicated November guide labels in-app payments Supported (new raw lines 206-213). These labels and the dated Android announcement establish no particular SDK implementation or account enablement. The aggregate API rows still omit Scalapay. Reorganized labels and pricing or acceptance links are presentation/navigation. Retain both raw captures and the reciprocal Stripe BNPL concept and acceptance guide routes.
